Both sides and the record agree on the shape of this trip, and they differ only on how much is owed. The recommended route was Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, Ang Mo Kio Ave 1, Bishan Road, Marymount Road, Thomson Road, at 6.7 km. The platform's recorded distances show the vehicle actually travelled 8.3 km, so the deviation is 1.60 km (8.3 minus 6.7), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets. The driver-device trace confirms the vehicle went via Braddell Road and Toa Payoh Lorong 6 rather than Marymount Road; per POL-RD-22 the trace shows which route was taken and when, and is not used to re-measure the distance. There is only one departure and one rejoin on the record, so nothing beyond the 1.60 km is attributable to the driver on this trip. Both driver-side and rider-side claims on the ceiling are therefore accepted: the deviation is 1.60 km and cannot be stretched toward the rider's 'about $3' impression. The reroute was not traffic-justified. The LTA traffic record for the recommended Marymount Road segment, valid 07:39:02-09:09:02 and so squarely covering the 08:09-08:30 trip, reports advisory type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure, and speed bands 4-5 throughout; the derived justifies_reroute value is false. Under POL-RD-23 a driver's assertion of traffic without such data does not justify the reroute, so your explanation, driver, that Marymount Road 'every morning sure jam one', cannot carry it. Nor was the rider informed. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat, or verbally with a trip call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log holds exactly two messages, both sent before the rider boarded (08:06:32 and 08:07:02) and both about where the car was parked; the trip record's messages_during_trip and in_app_calls are empty, so nothing was sent or said at the 08:16:41 deviation point or afterwards, and the record carries no call recording. Your own statement, driver, records that you didn't think you needed to say. On POL-RD-24's matrix this is row (d): the reroute was not traffic-justified and the deviation exceeds 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That is the deviation distance 1.60 km times the fare ledger's per-km rate of 0.72 SGD, with no surge applied to the excess distance fare and rounded to the cent: 1.15 SGD. The fare ledger reconciles line by line to the 15.97 SGD charged (base 2.80 + distance 5.98 + time 3.78 + surge 2.51 + platform fee 0.90, tolls 0.00), and the policy does not return the surge, the time fare or the rest of the total, so the rider's request for the full contested sum is not granted and the rider's own claim correctly limits the ask to 1.15 SGD. Rider and Driver, the claim is decided on the recorded route and distances. The recommended route was New Upper Changi Road, Bedok Road, Upper East Coast Road and Marine Parade Road, 4.6 km. The route actually driven was New Upper Changi Road, Jalan Bilal, Siglap Road, Upper East Coast Road and Marine Parade Road, 5.2 km. The trip record and GPS fixes support the rider's account that the vehicle left Bedok Road at Jalan Bilal and rejoined at Siglap Road. Under POL-RD-22 the deviation is the recorded actual distance minus the recorded optimal distance: 5.2 km minus 4.6 km equals 0.60 km. POL-RD-22 sets a 1.0 km tolerance, so this deviation is within tolerance. The GPS trace's 4.315 km figure is not used to re-measure distance under POL-RD-22; it shows the route taken only. The LTA traffic advisory for Bedok Road during the trip window reports type NONE, no incident, roadwork or closure, and speed bands 4-6, so POL-RD-23 does not justify the reroute. The chat log is complete and contains no in-trip notice or acknowledgment of the deviation, and there is no call recording, so POL-RD-21's notice requirement was not met. Even so, because the deviation is 1.0 km or less, POL-RD-24(e) applies: a not-traffic-justified deviation within tolerance gives NO_ACTION. The excess distance fare on POL-RD-24's formula would be 0.60 km x 0.72 SGD per km, which is 0.43 SGD, not the 2.00 SGD claimed, and it is not payable within tolerance. The 9.42 SGD metered fare stands. NO_ACTION is party-relative and leaves the present state in place, with no refund to the rider and no driver compensation. The disputed value is 2.00 SGD and neither profile has a fraud flag; POL-RD-25 requires 0.80 confidence for a route deviation and the confidence here is 0.95 on complete weight-1.0 artifacts. No clause produces a referral.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

To the rider and the driver: after testing both sides' claims against the record, part of the trip charge is returned — 1.01 SGD — and the rest of the charge stands.

How far the vehicle went. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation from the platform's own recorded distances: actual 9.5 km less recommended 8.1 km = 1.40 km (EV-TRIP-05004). That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so the deviation is real and material. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05004) shows which roads were used — Clementi Avenue 6 and Commonwealth Avenue West across the 08:42:55 to 08:53:16 window — but POL-RD-22 says the trace is not used to re-measure distance, so the 1.40 km figure from the trip record governs. Both sides' claims on this point are accepted.

Whether the rider was told. POL-RD-21 requires notice by in-app chat (or a recorded verbal notice) before or at the deviation. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05004) carries only two messages, both sent before the trip started and both about the meeting point; the record shows no messages and no calls during the trip, and the driver's own statement on file concedes he forgot to inform. The rider's single 'Ok' was an answer to a pickup message six minutes before the deviation and is not acknowledgment of it. Both sides' claims are accepted on this point.

Whether traffic justified the reroute. The LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05004-01) is a HEAVY_TRAFFIC type, which POL-RD-23 counts as admissible congestion. It is on the Pan-Island Expressway, the road the recommended route uses; its stated stretch (PIE towards Changi, after Clementi Avenue 6 exit to Clementi Road exit) is the recommended route's own segment, travelled in the direction of this trip; and it is valid 08:15:42 to 09:27:22, overlapping the trip window. The driver left the recommended route at 08:42:55 exactly at the Clementi Avenue 6 exit where that congestion begins. On the advisory's own road, direction and location read against the recorded route, the reroute was a response to real congestion and is traffic-justified under POL-RD-23.

The refund. POL-RD-24's matrix applies. The applicable row is (b): traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. This is why the driver's reliance on the justification does not avoid a refund, and the rider's request is scaled to what the policy provides. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.01 SGD (EV-FARE-05004). The rider's claim text asks for 4.00 SGD; the fare record does not support that figure, and POL-RD-24 caps the recovery at 1.01 SGD. The single ERP charge of 1.00 SGD was incurred at 08:40:36, more than two minutes before the vehicle left the recommended route, so it was incurred on the recommended stretch and is not part of the excess — the driver's claim on this is accepted.

The outcome is the same whether the traffic question is answered for the driver (row (b)) or against him (row (d)): both award the excess distance fare of 1.01 SGD. Nothing this case needs is missing or impaired, so POL-GEN-26 does not send it to a human reviewer: the deviation distance comes from a COMPLETE trip record, the notification position from a COMPLETE chat log and call list, the traffic data from a COMPLETE advisory, and the fare from a COMPLETE payments ledger. The contested amount is 4.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither party carries a fraud flag (POL-GEN-01, POL-GEN-22); and the confidence here is 0.9, above the 0.80 POL-RD-25 requires for a route deviation. No referral clause fires on this case.

Both sides' claims turn on four facts, and the record settles them.

1. Deviation (POL-RD-22). The platform's own recorded distances are 11.4 km driven against a 10.0 km recommended route — a deviation of 1.40 km, above the 1.0 km tolerance. Both parties agree on this and I accept it. The GPS trace's 9.652 km is not used to re-measure distance: POL-RD-22 says the trace shows which route was taken and when, not how long it was.

2. Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). EV-ADVIS-05003-01 (weight 1.0) records an ACCIDENT on the Central Expressway (CTE) towards SLE, after the Balestier Road exit, valid 18:37:44 to 19:49:44 — overlapping the trip window (the trip ran 18:49:44 to 19:12:44). The recommended route runs Raffles Quay – CTE – Braddell Road – Upper Serangoon Road, i.e. northbound on the CTE past the Balestier Road exit and on to Braddell Road; the incident lies on that stretch of the recommended route and in the same direction of travel. The advisory's derived block expressly leaves the intersection question to the tribunal on road, direction and location against the trip, and on those it intersects. The reroute is therefore traffic-justified. The rider's submission that the intersection is undetermined and that only the driver's own message ties the advisory to the route is rejected: the route geometry ties it, independently of the message, so POL-GEN-26 does not arise and no escalation is required.

3. Notice and agreement (POL-RD-21). The driver messaged the rider in-app at 18:57:46 (delivered 18:57:48, read 18:58:03), explaining the CTE accident and proposing the Bendemeer Road exit; the rider replied at 18:58:26 'Ok sure, thanks for telling'. The platform's deviation event is recorded at 19:00:36. Notice therefore preceded the manoeuvre, and POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. The rider's separate argument that agreement cannot cure an unjustified reroute does not bite, because the reroute is justified.

4. Refund matrix (POL-RD-24). On those findings row (a) applies exactly — traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km — and row (a) pays no refund. The rider's row (d) claim fails for want of the 'not traffic-justified' condition. For completeness, the excess distance fare would in any event be 1.40 km x 0.72 SGD per km = 1.01 SGD, not the 4.50 SGD claimed, because POL-RD-24 excludes the 1.3 surge multiplier; that figure is not payable here. The realised duration (23 min against a 20.2 min optimal) does not move the case out of row (a).

Outcome and confidence. The contested amount is 4.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so an AI ruling is final; POL-RD-25 requires confidence of 0.80, and every artifact carrying the deciding facts (EV-TRIP-05003, EV-CHAT-05003, EV-ADVIS-05003-01) carries weight 1.0. My confidence is 0.85. NO_ACTION means the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands — the metered fare of 22.60 SGD charged at 19:12:50, with nil refunded. No clause of the policy produces a referral on these facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

What the record shows. The app's recommended route was 12.1 km (Punggol Central, TPE, KPE, Paya Lebar Road); the route actually driven was 13.8 km, because the driver left the recommended route at the TPE / Upper Serangoon Road exit and ran down Upper Serangoon Road before rejoining at Paya Lebar Road. The deviation is 1.70 km (13.8 - 12.1), above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. Both distances are the platform's own recorded figures on a complete trip record (EV-TRIP-05005, weight 1.0), so the deviation is established and the tolerance rows of POL-RD-24 (rows (c) and (e)) are closed.

The informing duty. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to tell the rider of a reroute by in-app chat before or at the point of deviation. The event log in EV-TRIP-05005 times the departure from the recommended route at 10:21:30, and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05005, weight 1.0) places the vehicle off-route from the 10:21:38 fix. The driver's message MSG-05005-003 was sent at 10:24:30 - about three minutes after the deviation had already begun - so the notice was not given before or at the point of deviation. The rider's 'ok noted' at 10:25:00 shows he did not object, but it cannot make a late notice timely: row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the rider to have been informed as well as agreed, and the informing limb was not met. The driver's account that he informed the passenger 'before I changed route' is contradicted by those timestamps and by the empty in-app call list, so I do not follow it. The driver's argument that notice given while the deviation was still running is notice 'at the point of deviation' is rejected: the clause fixes the point of deviation as the moment of leaving the route.

Traffic justification. The LTA record (EV-ADVIS-05005-01, weight 1.0) shows a VEHICLE_BREAKDOWN on the KPE, in the direction of travel, valid 09:59:38 to 10:54:38 on the trip date - a type POL-RD-23 admits as an 'incident' and a window that spans the trip (10:14:38-10:38:08) and lies on the KPE stretch the recommended route uses. I read that as traffic justification, which puts the case on row (b) of POL-RD-24. Even if the advisory were read as sitting past the point at which the recommended route leaves the KPE, the case would fall on row (d): both rows return the excess distance fare, so the outcome does not turn on it, nothing needs escalating under POL-GEN-26, and the rider's point that the refund is the same either way is accepted.

The amount. POL-RD-24 measures the refund as the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.70 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.564, rounded to the cent, 1.56 SGD (EV-FARE-05005; per_km_rate_sgd 0.92, distance_charged_km 13.8, total_charged 23.04, refund_issued_sgd 0.0, and the ledger's own derived excess_distance_fare_sgd of 1.56). The 5.00 SGD claimed is the amount asked back, not the fare attributable to the deviation, and the whole trip fare is not returnable because the rider was carried to the destination and most of the route was as recommended; a full refund is not a value this category licenses. The driver's point that the claim cannot exceed 1.56 SGD is therefore accepted as to quantum.

Confidence and who decides. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; neither profile carries a fraud flag (EV-RPROF-05005, EV-DPROF-05005); and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is switched off, so an AI ruling is competent at the 0.80 confidence this category requires. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts is at full weight (1.0), and I hold the ruling at 0.85. No clause produces a referral in this case, and no amount is due to the driver.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

This dispute is decided on the platform's own recorded distances, and it comes down to a single number: the recommended route was 7.3 km (Yishun Avenue 2 – Yishun Avenue 1 – Seletar Road – Sengkang West Avenue) and the driver travelled 8.3 km (via Yio Chu Kang Road and Jalan Kayu, rejoining at Sengkang West Avenue). The difference is exactly 1.00 km. POL-RD-22 (Measuring the deviation, v2.1 1.4) sets the distance as trip_record.actual_distance_km minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km — that is, 8.3 – 7.3 = 1.00 km — and provides that a deviation of 1.0 km or less is within tolerance. 1.00 km is therefore within tolerance, at the line but inside it.

The reroute was not traffic-justified. The only traffic data on file is the LTA advisory for the recommended Seletar Road segment, both directions, covering 12:51–14:21 on the trip date (the trip window). It records type NONE — no congestion, no incident, no closure — and POL-RD-23 (Traffic justification) justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended segment shows congestion, an incident or a closure. NONE is not one of the types that clause admits. The driver's stated reason, that Jalan Kayu is smoother, is a road preference, not a traffic justification the policy recognises.

That places the case squarely in row (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix (v2.1 1.3): not traffic-justified, deviation 1 km or less — no refund, within tolerance. Row (c) reaches the same result on the traffic-justified branch, so the outcome does not turn on the justification question. No refund is payable, and the present state stands.

On the claims: I accept the driver's points that the deviation is 1.00 km and within tolerance, that the GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance (the 34-fix trace measures 6.996 km and, under POL-RD-22, would understate the route's length), that the reroute was not traffic-justified, that neither tolerance row pays anything, and that no escalation is forced (the contested amount is 2.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band in which an AI ruling is final; neither profile carries fraud_flags of 1 or more; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is not in force because ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false and the trip record marks over_ai_limit false). I accept the rider's points that the deviation of 1.00 km is established on the platform's telemetry, that the reroute had no traffic justification, and that the driver did not notify the rider: the chat log is complete and contiguous with zero messages, the trip record carries no in-app calls, and POL-RD-21 treats a verbal notice with no recording as not established. That omission does not change the outcome, because no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix conditions a refund on notification where the deviation is 1 km or less.

I reject the rider's argument that the case should go to a human reviewer under POL-GEN-26 because the deviation sits exactly on the tolerance line and distances are recorded to one decimal place. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established because the evidence carrying it is missing or impaired. Here nothing is missing or impaired: every artifact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, the two recorded distances the clause's own test reads are both present, and that test defines 'within tolerance' as 1.0 km or less. A test that runs on complete evidence and returns a result decides the limb; the possibility that rounding conceals a slightly larger true figure is speculation, not an impaired reading. The rider's fallback that the excess distance fare of 0.72 SGD (1.00 km × 0.72 SGD/km) is refundable only arises if the deviation is over 1 km, which it is not.

The disputed amount of 2.50 SGD is not collected and not refunded; the metered fare of 12.65 SGD stands as charged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: this route-deviation case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves on it now. The SGD 16.97 metered fare stays charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and is held; nothing is refunded to the rider at this stage. Here is why.

What the record settles.
(1) The deviation. The trip ran 10.9 km against a recommended 9.6 km, so the deviation is 1.30 km, over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 fixes that on the platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05014, weight 1.0, complete), not on the sparse 9.226 km trace, so no 'within tolerance' outcome is available. The rider is right on this point.
(2) Notice. The driver's in-app message MSG-05014-003 was sent at 21:19:56 and read at 21:20:23, before the vehicle left the route at 21:22:26, and it gave a brief reason. POL-RD-21's notice limb is met by the chat, and no call recording is needed. The driver is right on this point, and the rider accepts it.
(3) Traffic justification. I find the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05014-01 intersects the recommended route, so POL-RD-23 is satisfied. It is an ACCIDENT (an admissible incident type) on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 21:06-22:16, which covers the trip window 21:16-21:38. The recommended route runs on the KPE (Stadium Boulevard, KPE, Hougang Avenue 3, Hougang Avenue 10), and the trip record shows the vehicle leaving that route at exactly the KPE / MacPherson Road exit (21:22:26) while 'recommended KPE' - so the recommended route continues on the KPE past that exit, which is precisely where the advisory sits. The rider's contrary argument, that intersection is not established because the artifact's derived field is null, is rejected: that field is left for me to decide from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip, and they line up. This matters because it rules out POL-RD-24 rows (d) and (e) and with them the rider's claim that the excess distance fare is refundable as of right.

What the record does not settle - the open question.
(4) Whether the rider agreed. POL-RD-24(a) (no refund) needs the deviation to have been both notified and agreed, and POL-RD-21 makes it 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The only acknowledgment on record is MSG-05014-004 (21:20:41): 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah'. That chat log, EV-CHAT-05014, is IMPAIRED: issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight_multiplier 0.85, because the message mixes assent with a condition on the fare. It therefore does not cleanly confirm acknowledgment. Read one way the rider yielded the routing choice to the driver; read the other she attached a fare condition she says was broken. Row (a) is not made out, row (b) fails because she was in fact informed, and no other row of POL-RD-24 fits - which is the case POL-RD-24 sends to human review under POL-GEN-26. The driver's read of the message as plain acceptance, and the rider's read of it as an objection, are each more than this record can establish.
(5) Confidence. My confidence may not exceed the weight of the artifact carrying that decisive fact (POL-GEN-02(2)): the rider's acknowledgment/objection is carried only by EV-CHAT-05014 at 0.85, and the driver's counterparty statement (self-serving, made the next day) carries no weight and cannot lift it. Because the rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value, and POL-RD-25 will not let a route-deviation ruling stand below it. So even had I read the reply as assent, a NO_ACTION ruling could not stand; the driver's alternative argument that the outcome is at most 'no refund' is therefore only half right - it is human review, not a final no-action.

Money and referrals. The rider asks 4.20 SGD; the most POL-RD-24 can ever award on these facts is the excess distance fare, 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD without surge (EV-FARE-05014's own derived figure), but on an escalation no amount is refunded or newly collected - the fare is held. No referral is added: no clause in this category produces one.

Question for the reviewer: whether MSG-05014-004 was an agreement to the reroute or an objection to it, and, if conditional, whether 'dun charge me more ah' should leave the metered fare as charged or move it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

The deviation is measured under POL-RD-22 on the platform's recorded distances, not on the sparse trace: the trip record shows 18.3 km actually driven against 15.7 km on the recommended route, a deviation of 2.60 km (16.6%), which is over the 1.0 km tolerance. The GPS trace is not used to re-measure distance, but it confirms which route was taken — the vehicle left the recommended Pan-Island Expressway routing at the Pasir Ris Drive 3 / TPE slip road at 14:18:56, ran the TPE and then Braddell Road, and rejoined at Toa Payoh Lorong 6 at 14:40:41.

On traffic justification (POL-RD-23), the driver's explanation does not hold. The only advisory in the record is a ROADWORK on the PIE (towards Tuas) after Tampines Avenue 10 exit, and its validity window is 2026-09-05 23:00 to 2026-09-06 05:00 — the trip ran 14:16–14:42, so the advisory does not overlap the trip window and does not justify the reroute. POL-RD-23 is explicit that a driver's bare assertion of traffic, with no overlapping traffic data, does not justify a reroute. The driver's statement of roadworks is therefore noted but not accepted as a justification.

On notice (POL-RD-21), the chat log is contiguous with 0 messages, the trip record's in-app calls and messages_during_trip are empty, and there is no call recording in the record. A verbal notice with no recording cannot be established. The driver did not give recorded notice of the deviation.

Applying the POL-RD-24 matrix: the deviation is over tolerance, so rows (c) and (e) are closed; row (a) requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, which the empty chat log forecloses; and the reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case falls in row (d) — not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km — which refunds the excess distance fare in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 2.60 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.87 SGD, rounded to the cent. This is the whole monetary remedy the matrix provides; it is not the 6.00 SGD claimed, because POL-RD-24 returns the excess distance fare and not the trip fare, and it is not a NO_ACTION, because the deviation exceeded tolerance with no traffic justification. The rider is carrying the charge (total_charged 21.56 SGD, refund_issued_sgd 0.0), so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.87 SGD returns that part of the trip's charge.

On who decides: the contested amount is 6.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag and no safety flag is set, so the AI ruling is final on that clause; POL-RD-25's own 0.80 confidence requirement is met, and its extra 2 km limb is switched off because route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false. Every artifact this ruling rests on — the trip record, the GPS trace, the fare breakdown and the traffic advisory — is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so no fact is left unestablished and POL-GEN-26 does not require escalation.

This dispute concerns trip TRP-05016 (7 Sep 2026), on which SGD 1.68 was refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver after the rider's route complaint. The question is whether that refund stands. It does.

Deviation. POL-RD-22 (v2.1 1.4) measures the deviation from the platform's recorded distances: actual 9.9 km minus recommended 8.3 km = 1.60 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance (v2.1 1.3). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05016) shows which route was taken and when; it is not used to re-measure the distance.

Traffic. POL-RD-23 (v2.1 1.4) is satisfied on this record. LTA advisory LTA-TI-260907-3222 (EV-ADVIS-05016-01, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) reports HEAVY_TRAFFIC — one of the congestion types POL-RD-23 admits — on the CTE towards SLE after the Bukit Timah Road exit, valid 17:57 to 19:12, which overlaps the trip window (18:22:37 to 18:43:37). That stretch of the CTE, from the Bukit Timah Road exit towards Braddell Road, is part of the recommended route (Victoria Street, CTE, Braddell Road, Upper Thomson Road), so the advisory intersects the recommended route, and EV-TRIP-05016 shows the vehicle leaving that route at the very point the advisory names, the CTE / Bukit Timah Road exit, at 18:27:35. The driver was entitled to reroute in response to that congestion (POL-RD-21).

Notice. POL-RD-21 also requires the driver to tell the rider of the deviation by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation. That did not happen. The chat log (EV-CHAT-05016) holds only two messages, both sent before the trip started and both about the pickup (18:21:17 and 18:21:57); EV-TRIP-05016's in-trip message list and in_app_calls are empty, and there is no call recording. A verbal notice with no recording cannot be established (POL-RD-21, POL-GEN-26). The driver's reason — that he did not want to wake a sleeping passenger — is not an exception the clause provides.

Result. Row (b) of POL-RD-24 applies: traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — refund of the excess distance fare. That is 1.60 km x 1.05 SGD/km = 1.68 SGD without surge (POL-RD-24, v2.1 1.3), exactly the sum already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver.

On the driver's request that the case go to a human: refused. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule needs cannot be established, and POL-RD-25 (v2.1 6.2) allows an AI route-deviation ruling at 0.80 confidence or more. The one point the advisory's derived block leaves open — whether it intersects the recommended route — is one POL-RD-23 expressly asks the Judge to decide from the advisory's road, direction and location, and on that material it does intersect. In any event it cannot change the outcome: row (b) (traffic-justified) and row (d) (not traffic-justified) both refund the same excess distance fare, so nothing material is left unestablished.

The rider's observation that the trip took 21.0 minutes against the recommended 17.6 minutes does not alter the matrix; the refund turns on justification, notification and agreement only.

Accordingly the SGD 1.68 already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver stands. No driver compensation and no referrals.

To both parties. This is a route-deviation case (POLICY-ROUTE-DEVIATION v7.0.0, carrying Policy v2.1). It produces no money outcome: it goes to a human reviewer, and the 0.86 SGD now refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver's earnings is held pending that review.

What is established. On the platform's recorded distances, which POL-RD-22 requires be used, the deviation is actual 13.2 km minus optimal 12.0 km = 1.20 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance; the GPS trace is used only for which route was taken, not to re-measure distance. The excess distance fare is 1.20 x 0.72 = 0.86 SGD (POL-RD-24). Rows (c) and (e) of the POL-RD-24 matrix are therefore out, as both sides agree.

No AI ruling is issued. POL-RD-25 allows one only at a confidence of 0.80 or more, and the record does not carry the decisive fact. For the reviewer: the open question is whether the driver gave a verbal warning at the Braddell Road turn-off before or at 20:54:05, which only a trip call recording could establish on this record.

The result is the same if the traffic question fell the other way, because row (c) (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation 1 km or less) also returns no refund, so nothing turns on the driver's account of a queue at the TPE/PIE exit.
